subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own first-class Docker instance create/list/delete/update commands, or should multi-instance Docker remain documented manual Compose/profile operation for now?
rationale: The requested change creates official operator UX and persistent lifecycle semantics across Docker, config/state/workspace roots, ports, Compose names, update, deletion, and sandbox boundaries; source inspection shows no existing implementation to clean up automatically.

options.title: Sponsor a minimal core design
options.body: Approve a narrow design for named Docker instances with identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

options.title: Keep manual primitives for now
options.body: Leave this as a design backlog item while relying on the current multi-gateway docs, env variables, Docker setup script, Docker Compose project naming, and ClawDock helpers.

options.title: Route to external wrapper first
options.body: Ask contributors to maintain a wrapper or ClawHub package unless they can identify a missing core API that blocks safe external implementation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a minimal core design
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow design for named Docker instances with identity, ports, persistence, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product-scope choice about whether Docker lifecycle belongs in core, and this handle appears in adjacent multi-gateway product work while the code history is shared across Docker contributors.
